incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGER: High user-reported quality regressions for 'chat/generic' starting 2024-11-02T14:25Z. Severity: P2. Affected customers: 3 (trial + 2 mid-market). Metric spike: QA-failure-rate +18% over baseline. route_policy_id=rp-cost-pref-02
maya (oncall-sre): I'm on it, grabbing sigterm window and starting triage. Any initial alerts from runtime?
owen (eng-runtime): seeing elevated 'low_confidence' flags and a jump in requests routed to variant tiny-gen-lite-us-west1 (cheap variant). Normal is ~5% traffic, right now ~72% to tiny-gen-lite-us-west1.
eva (prod-ops): customers reported more hallucinations and truncated completions, screenshots incoming via Zendesk.
sam (eng-ml): that variant has lower params/quant and known quality delta. Why would routing prefer it? Check cost-policy weights.
diane (product): customer impact: 2 customers have opened urgent tickets, one flagged as 'investigate or pause'. We should consider mitigation that avoids user-facing regressions.
jen (support): customer A (acme) just posted examples where outputs were factual but missing key constraints. They're asking for rollback.
maya (oncall-sre): snapshotting routing table and policy state now: `curl -s https://controlplane.local/policies/rp-cost-pref-02` -> response shows `budget_mode: aggressive`, `fallback_order: [cheapest, compatible, fastest]`. That fallback_order looks reversed.
owen (eng-runtime): oh — fallback_order was recently flipped in a deploy yesterday via infra-config-PR#482. I see commit `set-default-fallback: cheapest-first` on 2024-11-01 21:06 UTC.
sam (eng-ml): that explains it. Cheap-first will prefer tiny-gen variants even if quality drops. We should revert to `quality-first` or ensure thresholds.
eva (prod-ops): mitigation options: 1) revert policy, 2) override route to pin to baseline variant (gen-std), 3) throttle cheap variants. Which do we want for fastest user relief?
maya (oncall-sre): do a fast override: `POST /routes/override {route: chat/generic, variant: gen-std, ttl: 3600}` — I'll apply and watch.
sre-bot: ACTION: route override initiated by maya — id=ovr-67322 status=pending
maya (oncall-sre): override succeeded, traffic shifting now. tiny-gen-lite-us-west1 dropping from 72% -> 8% in last 2 minutes. Customer errors dropping in realtime metrics.
jen (support): acme confirms partial improvement. Still seeing some degraded responses but much better. They're appreciative.
diane (product): can we keep a canary on gen-std and shadow-test tiny-gen-lite for cost metrics but prevent user-facing traffic?
sam (eng-ml): yes, set tiny-gen-lite to shadow mode: `PATCH /variants/tiny-gen-lite {routing: shadow}`. I'll run evals on the queued requests.
owen (eng-runtime): root cause summary: config change flipped fallback priority during a config rollout. Policy lacked explicit quality floor checks, so cost led to aggressive selection of the low-cost variant causing a quality regression loop.
maya (oncall-sre): paging note: there was also a regional fallback loop — US-west exceeded concurrency and routed to cheapest in EU which then routed back due to mismatch in compatibility tags, causing oscillation for ~7 min. Need fix.
eva (prod-ops): action items for immediate fix: 1) revert fallback_order to quality-first (PR in progress), 2) add quality_floor threshold in policy engine (require >=Q0.85), 3) add canary gates for config rollouts.
sam (eng-ml): will add metric gating for model selection: `model_q_score` and `bleu/rouge` thresholds tied to route selection. I'll open PR.
owen (eng-runtime): deploying hotfix to policy-evaluator to prefer regional latency when quality within delta. Rolling to 3 nodes now.
sre-bot: DEPLOY: policy-evaluator hotfix rolled to prod by owen — rollout_id=rlt-9901 status=done
maya (oncall-sre): monitoring: user QA-failure-rate trending back down to baseline over 14 minutes. Logging retention collected for 30m window.
diane (product): customer outreach: Jen, can you send templated note to affected customers explaining rollback and next steps? Offer credits.
jen (support): On it. Sending now.
maya (oncall-sre): handoff: I'll keep this in my queue for 30 minutes, then hand to eng-runtime for postmortem. Tagging @owen for long-term follow-up.
owen (eng-runtime): got it. I'll coordinate the postmortem and include regression tests for fallback-order and regional routing tags.
sam (eng-ml): also adding a synthetic test that runs every deploy to ensure cheap variants don't exceed quality delta > 10% from baseline on standard prompt set.
eva (prod-ops): severity update: downgrade to P3 — user impact mitigated. Creating incident report ticket INC-2024-8775.
maya (oncall-sre): closing pager for now. Will file timeline in postmortem doc. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
incident-bot: Incident closed by maya (oncall-sre). Duration: 00:42:17. Link: https://incidents.redwood.internal/INC-2024-8775
